current_answer: AI has genuine customers and useful products. Some financing contracts can protect lenders even when an AI investment disappoints. Neither establishes that the whole build-out—or the prices paid to own it—will earn enough back. The evidence supports a real expansion with uneven investment returns and concentrated financing vulnerabilities, not a uniformly unsupported AI economy or an inevitable credit collapse.
summary: Real customer value. Uneven returns. The financial question is who keeps enough cash, for long enough.
uncertainty: Independent customers renewing at nonsubsidized prices, durable cash margins after full costs, and successful repayment and replacement across delivered investment cohorts would weaken the concern. Weak retention, greater dependence on fresh financing and poorer collateral recovery together would strengthen it—even if technical performance keeps improving.
